lede: The dollar index pushed to its highest since April 2025 as markets price a roughly 94% chance of a Fed hike in December and US 10-year yields hold near 5.15%. Gold slipped toward $3,860 and the euro hovered near a 19-month low, while crypto steadied after a bruising weekend.

focus.text: Firm dollar and 5.15% Treasury yields push gold toward $3,863, below its 3,891.6 pivot and near last week's 3,852 low; Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 20:00 TRT.
Fed-hike bets and the widest US–euro rate gap of the year keep the pair around 1.102, below its 1.1039 pivot; Empire State (16:30) and Warsh (20:00) are today's risks.

technicals.indicators: Below 20-day MA (~4,023) · weekly declining channel, closed below its midline · 3,736–3,705 = 127.2% ext. / 61.8% Fib confluence
technicals.note: Gold is consolidating just above last week's 3,852 low after breaking 3,870, with rallies capped so far below the 3,923–4,001 area.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 33 · riding the lower Bollinger band (~1.1030; mid-band 1.1160) · well below 100-day SMA (~1.1400)
technicals.note: The pair is pressing the 1.10 handle at a 19-month low, extending the series of lower highs that began with the August reversal.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 22.5 (oversold) · below 200-week MA (~67,990) · MACD histogram negative
technicals.note: Bitcoin bounced from Sunday's ~62,000 low back toward 65,000 but remains below the 200-week average it lost last week.

technicals.indicators: Below 50-week (~2,280) and 200-week (~2,560) SMAs · lower highs and lower lows since the 2,807 rejection
technicals.note: Ether lost the 1,853 shelf last week and is trading inside the gap down toward the 1,571–1,385 historical demand zone.

news.text: Futures price about a 94% chance of a 25bp Fed hike in December and ~6% for 50bp; around four hikes are priced by next September.
The dollar index reached ~103.4, its strongest since April 2025; USD/JPY sits near 160, close to where intervention is believed to have occurred earlier this year.
October data disappointed: industrial output +4.8% y/y (exp. 5.3%), retail sales +0.4% (exp. 0.8%), fixed-asset investment −8.1% year to date.
Japan's economy shrank at a 0.1% annualised pace in Q3, missing forecasts for modest growth.
Brent eased to about $95.4 as Hormuz flows near pre-war levels and the IEA now sees a Q4 surplus of roughly 1.7m bpd.
Bitcoin recovered toward $65,000 after dipping to about $62,000 on Sunday, its weakest since July; the Fear & Greed index sits at 10.
US spot bitcoin ETFs logged seven straight sessions of net outflows through 13 Nov, totalling roughly $1.9bn.
CryptoQuant says wallets holding over 1,000 BTC added about 47,000 BTC into the drop, while ~73% of short-term holder supply is underwater.
KAVA sank close to 40% in a day after about 55.2m tokens were abnormally borrowed and dumped through Kava Lend.
Around 64,000 bitcoin mining rigs were reportedly hijacked, diverting roughly 13 EH/s of hashrate to the OCEAN pool.
CRO (~2.3% of supply, ≈$51m) and ARB unlock today; LayerZero's ZRO releases ~3.7% (≈$35m) on Friday.

upcoming.note: Consensus ~0.0–0.2% m/m after 0.8%; a strong print would feed 50bp talk.

upcoming.event: Nvidia Q3 results (after US close Tue)
upcoming.note: Revenue est. ~$109bn, EPS ~$2.47; first report under interim CEO Kress.
Exp 3.6% y/y, prev 3.5%; key for a December BoE hike.
Rates held 3.75–4.00% with two dissents for a hike.
Read on US consumer; guided adj. EPS $0.62–0.64.
Claims exp 200k; Philly Fed exp 19.2, prev 20.9.
Seen around 2.0%; shapes BoJ hike timing after weak GDP.

week_ahead.intro: A Fed on the verge of hiking again sets the tone: US retail sales and the FOMC minutes will test whether a 50bp move in December gains traction. Nvidia's first results since its CEO change and UK CPI round out a heavy week, with crypto still nursing a sharp sell-off.

themes.text: A December hike is nearly fully priced; retail sales, the minutes and Warsh's remarks decide whether 50bp re-enters the debate.
Q3 results on Tuesday night are the first under interim CEO Colette Kress and a test for AI-heavy indices.
Retail sales plus Walmart, Home Depot, Target and Lowe's earnings gauge US household demand.
UK CPI could cement a second BoE hike; weak Japanese GDP and China data contrast with tightening elsewhere.
Bitcoin trades below its 200-week average after seven days of ETF outflows; unlocks include CRO, ARB and ZRO.

events.note: Watch for hints on December size
